# wherdr v3 documentation

> wherdr is a web app to start coding agents on herdr-core (hc), follow their work and answer
> them from a phone. Read this index first, then only the section that answers your question.
> Links are relative to the repository root. A section that starts with "Needs:" makes sense only
> with the section it names: read that one too.

## Start here

- [Documentation home](docs/README.md): the list of pages, v3 and v2 only.
- [Community](docs/README.md#community): the wherdr Discord (https://discord.gg/ky36WYmtVE) for questions and feedback; bugs go to GitHub issues.
- [Overview](docs/overview.md#why-wherdr): what wherdr does for you.
- [How it works](docs/overview.md#how-it-works): wherdr's server, the hc socket, transcripts and the data folder.
- [herdr-core](docs/core.md): what v3 supports on hc, the reference for inventory, terminals and conversations.
- [First launch](docs/quick-start.md#quick-start): build, start and open wherdr from source; Settings › About shows `wherdr <version>+<commit> · herdr-core`; Alfred and the setup window set up a first project; then the Board, or Alfred.

## Install and update

- [Requirements](docs/installation.md#requirements): hc, Linux or macOS, Node.js 22 and Git; [Windows](docs/installation.md#on-windows-experimental) experimental, not supported yet (Files view and git changes call `sh`): hc via `install.ps1`, `HC_SOCKET` a named pipe `\\.\pipe\herdr-core-<user>-<session>.sock`, `npm.cmd` when PowerShell blocks `npm`.
- [The hc socket](docs/installation.md#the-hc-socket): the default `HC_SOCKET`: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/herdr-core/<session>.sock` on Linux, `~/.local/state/herdr-core/<session>/<session>.sock` on macOS; session `default`.
- [v2 and v3 on one computer](docs/installation.md#v2-and-v3-on-one-computer): v2 and a by-hand v3 both default to port 7683; start v3 with `PORT=7684`.
- [A second v3 on one computer](docs/installation.md#a-second-v3-on-one-computer): a second v3 keeps its own pm folders (`WHERDR_PM_DIR`, `.wherdr/pm-<name>` from the install script for another `--name`); its uninstall removes them.
- [On macOS](docs/installation.md#on-macos): install by hand (the script needs systemd), the macOS socket path, a LaunchAgent, Keep awake.
- [Installation](docs/installation.md#installation): install v3 and run it as a service.
- [Keep it running](docs/installation.md#keep-it-running): run wherdr as a service (a systemd --user unit, a macOS LaunchAgent).
- [On-device dictation files](docs/installation.md#on-device-dictation-files): where the dictation models and read-aloud voices are fetched and kept.
- [Updating](docs/installation.md#updating): the version in Settings › About (with its commit), a banner for a newer 3.x release only (never a 2.x) with What's new (the release notes) and Update with Alfred, or update v3 by hand: `update.sh <version>` checks out the tag `v<version>` (never `git pull` in its detached checkout) and rolls back a build that does not answer; in a checkout of your own (macOS), `npm run build:aside` builds aside.
- [Update with an agent](docs/update-with-an-agent.md): the steps Alfred (or any agent) follows to update v3: find the unit, read the release's Upgrade notes, plan and your yes, back up DATA_DIR, update.sh <version> (checks out the tag v<version>, builds aside, keeps .output.prev, puts it back by itself when the new build does not answer with its version), run in the background with build.log watched (the build outlasts a command timeout) or, on macOS or in a checkout of your own, git checkout v<version>/npm ci/npm run build:aside (builds aside too), check /api/health, roll back on failure (.output.prev); never sudo without asking, never restart herdr-core.
- [Install with an agent](docs/install-with-an-agent.md): ready-to-paste prompts for an agent that installs or updates wherdr.
- [Release notes 3.0.0](docs/release-notes-3.0.0.md): what v3 brings to a v2 user: projects, board and coordinators (named after their project, row menu, Read/Act on other projects), New project with no template step, Tasks to review, Accept at any time, Notes, the merge queue and engine reliability, Alfred's one-card v2 import, quotas, phone fixes, the update banner (What's new, Update with Alfred, Upgrade notes); what changed (installed from the v3 branch beside v2, GitHub release only), what is gone, how to move; workspaces come in 3.1.
- [What v3 drops](docs/release-notes-3.0.0.md#gone-v2-only): what v3 drops compared with v2: Herdr sessions and plugin, the herdr-projects board, npm, Homebrew, Herdr plugin install, curl installer, Docker, one-tap update, worktrees, model pickers, split panes.
- [Migrate from v2](docs/migrate-from-v2.md): install v3 beside v2 and import its machines, settings and recent folders, nothing of herdr-projects: v3's service gets v2's board path and Alfred sets up its projects; the plan names them, and a v2 data folder with no service or running v2 is asked about.
- [What is imported](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#what-is-imported): what the v2 import brings over (v2's own machine becomes v3's local one in the machine tabs and groups), and what to redo.
- [Set up your v2 projects with Alfred](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#set-up-your-v2-projects-with-alfred): Alfred's first message offers to bring v2 projects over, reading the herdr-projects board then: one card lists them all (a checkbox each, a folder not found says why, Start their coordinators, and Turn on project management while it is off), and one Apply adds the checked ones and starts their coordinators, no workflow needed (each coordinator's first reply proposes a workflow); then per project its open tasks (under-way ones continue from their branch and PR); an optional handover note from the v2 coordinator and its autopilot goal go into the new coordinator's memory.md.
- [Auto-deploy from a build machine](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#auto-deploy-from-a-build-machine): build elsewhere and deploy to the server.
- [Fall back to v2](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#fall-back-to-v2): go back to v2, and [uninstall v3](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#uninstall-v3) (with an install's own pm folders); on v3, `herdr plugin install|update` and the `curl … | sh` installer change nothing and say how to install v3.
- [Install as an app](docs/phone.md#install-it-as-an-app): add wherdr to a phone's home screen or a desktop browser.
- [App start](docs/phone.md#app-start): Settings › Phone › App start, network first or saved copy first; after an update, a Reload banner and no reload by itself.

## Network and security

- [Tailscale setup](docs/networks.md#recommended-always-on-server--tailscale): reach wherdr from a phone over a tailnet with HTTPS.
- [Other private networks](docs/networks.md#other-private-networks): Headscale, NetBird, ZeroTier or WireGuard instead.
- [Security](docs/security.md#security): who may reach wherdr, the passkey lock, protected files (wherdr's data and settings, keys, agents' credentials, herdr-core's state but its uploads) and remote-shell risks.
- [Network access](docs/security.md#network-access): which networks wherdr answers, and `WHERDR_TRUSTED_NETWORKS`.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md#configuration): environment variables (`WHERDR_ROOT`: the install folder, where Alfred finds the running build's docs) and the data folder. [Appearance](docs/configuration.md#appearance): nine themes (wherdr Titanium default, Neon, Graphite; Claude Code, Codex, omp; Vesper, Gruvbox, Kanagawa), each dark and light, and a synced mode Dark (default) / Light / System (follows the device live); removed themes fall back to Titanium, Catppuccin Latte and omp Light open in Light mode. [Custom themes](docs/configuration.md#custom-themes): create from any theme with a live preview and contrast check, or edit it as JSON (a JSON tab validated live like an import: error with its line, Save disabled), synced, exported and imported as JSON; Alfred proposes one you describe as a card (preview, contrast check, Apply / Edit in editor / Cancel; `wherdr alfred theme propose`).
- [Settings beside the conversation](docs/configuration.md#settings-beside-the-conversation): on a computer window at least 1280 px wide, Settings opened from a conversation show as a side panel on the linked section, resizable from its left edge (drag, arrows, double-click for the default; width kept on the device); its section menu shows names from 560 px, icons with names on hover below (a button shows the names, kept on the device); Escape closes it, Open full page keeps the full page; `&target=<id>` scrolls to one setting and outlines it for a few seconds.

## Agent list

- [Alfred](docs/home.md#alfred): wherdr's assistant (its card looks selected only while its conversation is open), its agent (kept until you change it), name, home folder and memory; with no project, its first message and Home's empty list offer to set up the first one (with Alfred, in the setup window, or with the New › Project form, which Alfred opens on Settings › Projects › Add project), or, coming from v2, count its v2 projects not set up yet; one question per message (the name question after the offer); replies headed with its name, its start instructions a collapsed system line, never the title.
- [Agents on herdr-core](docs/home.md#agents-on-herdr-core): the live list, states and their counters (agent rows plus the tab's coordinators), quick answers, the sidebar's order and first load (skeletons until every section is read, then one paint; no sideways scroll: long titles and badges ellipsized, a thin scrollbar; a long press on a row opens its menu only, no text selection or iOS callout), and task agents named after their task (after a restart too), one row per task with a line per agent (its agent's icon, role, machine, last message; a reviewer's verdict as a short line, not JSON).
- [Coordinators](docs/home.md#coordinators): project coordinator rows under Alfred, with the project's colored key badge and the coordinator's name (the project's by default, renamable in the General tab and at setup), and their menu (open the board, project settings, autopilot with its on check, the same three first in their conversation header's ⋯ menu, rename inline, mute, Move to hidden / Move back, restart with another agent, stop after a confirm); their order by drag and drop (a ⠿ handle on hover, a long press on a phone, arrow keys on the handle), kept on the server; a collapsed Hidden group at the end (Show hidden (n) / Hide), filled by a drop or Move to hidden, a hidden one needing you showing in the main list until answered; a stopped one (its terminal ended) offers to resume its conversation or start a new one; one that never started shows Not started with Start (its saved agent), and after a failed start herdr-core's kind and message with Start again; coordinators and Tasks to review follow the machine tab (a project shows on the tabs holding its machines, a workspace member where its workspace does, Alfred on every tab); a workspace's coordinator is its workspace row (under its tab group: its coordinator's state, its members' and features' tasks working and waiting for you, its members' key badges (a small square on one waiting), a tap listing them with a link to each board and each one's counts; n waiting for you a link: one task's sheet, several the workspace's board or a member's Tasks to review; menu with Workspace settings, its board showing every member's tasks; reorder and Hidden as any coordinator).
- [Tasks to review](docs/home.md#tasks-to-review): Home's card, right under Alfred and above the coordinators, with the count of what waits for you on the tab's projects and the ids of the first ones as colored key badges on one line (… past it); a tap opens them one at a time.
- [Offered agents](docs/home.md#offered-agents): Settings › Agents, which programs every picker offers and in which order; a project's coordinator runs on Claude, Codex or omp (omp only when chosen: never the default while a Claude or Codex is offered; its tool list has no edit tool, but its shell can still write). [Named agents](docs/home.md#named-agents): Settings › Agents, a name for a command (an executable or wrapper script on the PATH and fixed options) of claude, codex or omp on chosen machines, for a second account or launch options; add, edit, remove, synced; never a secret (keys stay in the wrapper script, keychain example).
- [Machines as tabs](docs/home.md#machines-as-tabs): the machine tabs and their counts (rows and coordinators), their groups (deleting one puts its projects back to Automatic), which tabs show a project (its machines', a paused one only while its task runs, or its Shown in; notifications are not filtered, the board only on Follow machine tab), a machine's actions, and the offline machines' line with Reconnect (no machine chips while all are online).
- [New agents and tabs](docs/home.md#new-agents-and-tabs): the New sheet (its machine: the current tab's first online one, else the host, as on All; its folder browser a tree under home, loaded as folders open, Git marks, a path field), the + of a space's tabs, and renaming or closing a tab or a space.
- [Search](docs/home.md#search): one ⌘K / Ctrl+K palette for conversations, tasks, projects, settings and actions (New agent, New task, Tasks to review, Notes, Shortcuts); on a narrow list the header's Search moves into its ⋯ menu while Settings stays a button.
- [Notes panel](docs/home.md#notes): the conversation header's Notes button beside Search (first entry of its ⋯ menu when the header is narrow, after a coordinator's board, settings and autopilot; Mod+Alt+P): the agents' notes, read-only, beside the conversation or Home's list on a computer of 1280 px or more (resizable; stays open after a reload, on its linked file, per device), hidden on a page without it (board, settings) and back beside the next conversation, a sheet otherwise (an explicit open only, not reopened on reload); Follow tab by default (a muted line names the tab followed, another says when it has no note of its own), or All or one tab (a group or a machine shown as its own tab); checkboxes, project and custom badges, in-app links and links between notes; a linked file (plans/x.md) opens rendered in the panel with a back arrow, its relative links kept inside the notes folder; missing links muted with a tooltip; live updates; headings and `---` separators (a thin rule) in a note.
- [Inventory](docs/core.md#inventory): how terminals are placed in spaces and tabs, and how states are read.
- [Creating terminals and agents, machines](docs/core.md#creating-terminals-and-agents-machines): what the New sheet asks hc to run, and how hc reaches core machines.
- [Agent actions](docs/core.md#agent-actions): the agent's … menu: rename, keep after restart, answers, attachments.

## Conversation, terminal and files

- [Conversation and replies](docs/conversation.md): transcripts, every message's time (agent replies included, with the day for an earlier one, the full date on hover or tap), following new messages from the bottom, the working line (Claude's own verb *✻ Orbiting…*, omp's running step and time; *1 shell running in the background* once Claude's turn is over), one-tap answers, choice buttons (1 to 4, one alone is a confirm; an invalid block stays code), a `questions` card (up to 8 numbered questions of 2 to 4 options: one pick or Other… per question, digit and letter keys, one Send for all, one line per question (`1A Postgres`, `2B No, remove it`, your own words as typed), unanswered sent as `skip`; also in Tasks to review) and live task cards (`task KEY-12`, opens the task's sheet) from a `wherdr` code fence, proposed shell commands (Copy, ▷ Run on every block: *Running…* then *Ran at 16:42*, a live *You ran* card at its place in time, above messages sent while it runs, replaced by the transcript's entry; run while Claude works: its queued bubble alone until Claude runs it once at the turn's end), quoted replies, attachments (in the field: one square tile per photo, file or pasted text on one sideways-scrolling row that fades at the right edge while more follow: extension badge, preview (photo, a text's first lines, an icon), file name, size or lines, the upload's spinner, a refused one's reason until removed), sent messages: attachments on their own row above the bubble, on its side (photos as plain thumbnails, files and pasted text as the field's tiles without the cross, wrapping, photos past nine on a +N tile, a tap opens the viewer on the message's photos, a sent file's tap its path menu), photos as pictures also after Send now / Retry, shown at once from the device's copy, a failed image retried once then *Tap to reload*), messages sent while a wake is typed waiting for it instead of failing, dictation, and in-app links (`#/settings?section=…`, `#/board?task=…`), shown as labelled buttons, that open a place in wherdr.
- [Live status cards](docs/conversation.md#live-status-cards): a `wherdr` code fence of `status machine:<key>`, `status quota:claude|codex`, `status pr:<KEY>#<n>` or `status op:<task id>` lines shows live cards from wherdr's own data, refreshed every 15 s on screen, "unavailable" when the source is gone.
- [Places an agent opens for you](docs/conversation.md#places-an-agent-opens-for-you): `wherdr alfred ui open` / `wherdr pm ui open '<in-app link>'` shows a place on the device the user last used on the agent's conversation (Settings side panel on a wide computer, even for bare `#/settings`), says where (phone or computer), keeps the card in the reply (```wherdr `open <link>`), the one element for the place (a bar as wide as the message field only when the reply ends without it), only in a turn from the user, changing nothing; `ui open --target <id>` highlights one setting (`ui targets` lists the ids; a part of a project's sheet, `project.workflow|guards|autopilot`, takes `--project <KEY>`).
- [Terminal](docs/terminal.md): the real terminal, shared viewers, taking control, wheel scrolling of a program's fullscreen view (Claude Code) paced on its repaints and matched to the gesture, Split right and Split down (Mod+Alt+S, Mod+Alt+Shift+S; wherdr's own layout, synced across devices), Split with agent (the New agent sheet, the agent to the right), dragging the dividers to resize (double-click for 50/50).
- [Buttons an agent puts in its reply](docs/conversation.md#buttons-an-agent-puts-in-its-reply): `wherdr pm ui action resume|step|open <task>` adds a card with *Resume*, the step's own button (*Merge*, *Approve screenshots*) or *Open*; only the user's click runs it (`POST /api/ui/act`, never a token), through the task sheet's handlers, after checking the task still waits the same way (else *This changed since*, nothing runs); only in a turn from the user; the outcome shows on the card (an approved merge not ready yet: approved, merges once ready; a refused step action keeps the button with its reason). Settings: `wherdr alfred setting set <key> <value> --propose` adds a card (before → after, *Show me* highlights it, *Cancel*, *Apply*); only the user's Apply changes it, stale if the setting moved since; Alfred never applies a setting itself. Project changes: `wherdr alfred project add|template|guards|machine … --propose` or `coordinator start … --propose` adds the same card with the change's lines; Apply makes it only while its dry run still shows those lines. [What a card tells its agent](docs/conversation.md#what-a-card-tells-its-agent): Apply, Cancel or a failed apply (and a workflow or automation change answered) is typed into the proposer's conversation as a muted *From the card* row (`From the card: Applied: <summary>`, `Cancelled: …`, `Not applied: <why>`), so it goes on by itself (it may propose the next card; the click is never the user's yes to anything else); while it does not run, its next start's first message lists them. `wherdr pm ui show file <path>|shots <task>` shows a file of the agent's own folder or of one of its project's tasks' folders (`ABC-24/report.md` or its absolute path under the pm tasks folder; another project's task only within the coordinator's reach; never `..`) (an `.html` page runs in a sandboxed frame, Preview | Source, self-contained: inline CSS/JS/images and https CDN links, no files next to it, no fetch) or a task's screenshots (before/after) in the side panel (resizable by its left edge like Notes, width kept on the device), or a card then a sheet on a phone; it approves nothing.
- [Conversations on hc](docs/core.md#conversations): which agents open on their transcript and how it is read (Claude Code, Codex, Devin, Antigravity `agy`, Hermes Agent from its `state.db`, untested on a real Hermes; a local Codex on the shared app-server: its paginated daemon history, read-only, matched by title, rollout fallback), and text left unsent in Claude's input box (Send now loads at once, never sends twice, says why it failed; every send to Claude is checked in its box, idle or busy: a photo message is submitted once Claude shows its placeholders, or with its path when the photo stays a path (also one drawn over two lines), also inside a collapsed `[Pasted text #N]` (matched by its line count, also a one-line or text-only message; no `\` inside it ever reaches Claude; pasted once more first; at most 18 s from the paste, never left in the box, *Not sent* with Retry when the box never held it alone; *Sending… adding the photo* meanwhile on every device, updated live, showing the user's own text, run by the server whatever the page does), also when sent during a turn, Enter retried for about 16 s, also while Claude still shows Pasting… and after a wherdr restart mid-send, Send now's Enter too; *Sending…* with a loader until the transcript has it and *Not sent* only once the server gave up (WHR-471), never shown as read nor twice, waiting messages in sending order whichever list holds them, its photo placeholders and paths ignored when matched, never glued to the next message).
- [On a computer](docs/devices.md#on-a-computer): layout (Split right / Split down, Mod+Alt+S / Mod+Alt+Shift+S: a second shell in the same tab, Split with agent: a new agent to its right, in wherdr's own synced layout; drag a divider to resize, double-click for 50/50), the wherdr grid with animated packets behind the conversation (always on, still with reduced motion), terminal key bar and keyboard shortcuts (message history on the first or last wrapped line of the field; any shortcut can be changed in Settings › Shortcuts, with conflicts refused and Reset).
- [Files](docs/files.md): browse an agent's folder as a tree (folders read as they open, the preview beside it on a wide panel), preview text, Markdown, images, PDFs, videos and HTML pages (run sandboxed, Preview | Source), download; [one file shown alone](docs/files.md#one-file) (a conversation's path, `ui show file`) reads as a document: its name the window's title, folder · size and icon controls under it, full width at a readable line length, no glyph on inline code; which files a path in a conversation may open (home only while settings.json cannot be read), and where a relative one is found (agent's folder, repository, notes; a bare name not found: in the folders quoted before it in the same message).
- [On a phone](docs/devices.md#on-a-phone): touch controls and the phone keybar (order and hidden keys in Settings › Terminal, its preview under *Show me*).
- [On an iPad](docs/devices.md#on-an-ipad): the iPad layout.

## Project management

- [Getting started](docs/project-management.md#getting-started): the setup window, three steps (Turn on, with Let Alfred guide me a quieter button; Your project: folder, machine, visibility and the coordinator's agent and model (empty: the agent's default), kept as its default; Meet your coordinator: Start with… starts it and opens its conversation, its first message proposing how you work), no Back on the first step, no workflow or template to pick (the coordinator's first message proposes the first workflow, guards included; Alfred can copy another project's instead); a project counts as set up once its coordinator runs, with or without a workflow; step 3 says starting, asks with Answer its question, or runs, and Next waits until it runs; the coordinator's and Alfred's new folder trusted at their first start; what a project needs (git, and `origin` unless its workflow lands locally like vibe); the coordinator's own memory.md; Finish setup on the board; New › Project opens on adding one (a Project | Workspace switch at the top, Project by default, Workspace showing the [workspace form](docs/workspaces.md#creating-a-workspace); machine tabs, the machine's git repositories with a search, Or any folder with Browse; picking one fills name and key, editable, shown as ~/…; no template: the minimal default, its coordinator starts at once with the chosen agent and proposes a workflow; below, Restart a coordinator (with their number, collapsed by default) lists only those whose coordinator does not run, hidden when none, the agent picker after it; a wider sheet on a computer).
- [Projects](docs/project-management.md#projects): Settings › Projects, two sections: Workspaces (Add workspace in its header; each workspace's row with its member projects indented under it, folded or open with its chevron, open by default, kept on the device) then Projects (those outside any workspace; Add project (the New sheet's Project form, as New › Project; no Set up a project button) and Open the board in its header); compact rows (colored key badge, name, Public and machine on one line, the folder small under it, ellipsized), a tab filter (Follow tab by default, All, each home tab or tab group; kept on the device) and past 8 projects a search (name, key, folder; a member hit shows under its workspace, opened; nothing found offers Show all tabs; a ?project= link opens a hidden one) (grey blocks until it is read, Try again if that fails) and the project sheet's tabs (wide on a computer, General fields side by side), a close cross and a ⋯ menu side by side at its header's right; removing a project (⋯ menu) is refused while it has open tasks or, for a workspace, members; a project whose workflow cannot be read starts none of its tasks, its log says why once, and other projects' starts go on. A project added without git is treated as a git repository once its folder becomes one, at its next task or coordinator start or at Check again.
- [The coordinator's first conversation](docs/project-management.md#the-coordinators-first-conversation): on a project with no accepted workflow (tasks follow a minimal default, one type `task`: to do → work → done), the coordinator's first start sends it a first message: it reads the repository (stack, tests, CI, branches, PR host), introduces itself, sums up the project (or asks what to build) and, in that first reply, proposes a workflow with the guards that fit (often from a built-in example), its diff against the default, saying why (starting it counts as your request); then asks as choices what to change (stricter or lighter); setting suggestions once, never repeated; a wherdr issue or PR drafted for your yes; the first message waits until its session is ready (up to 10 minutes), coordinators started together start one after another, each outcome (sent, queued, not delivered and why) goes to the project's log (a send herdr-core did not confirm is never typed twice: not delivered, check before Send again), and one not delivered shows on its row, running or stopped (First message not delivered, Send again in its menu, a new conversation when its session ended), and to Alfred (coordinator resend); the next start gives it again.
- [General tab](docs/project-management.md#general): no Save button, every field saves by itself (a switch or pick at once, typed text after a pause or on blur, the key only on blur or Enter), a discreet Saved ✓ next to its label, an invalid or refused value's message under the field, the typed text kept; name, coordinator name (empty: the project's name, which follows a rename; also asked at setup), other projects this coordinator may act on (only those reached, Read or Act, with remove; Add picks another at Read), key (a new one also in wakes, notifications, logs, PR titles, `wherdr pm` outputs and new branches; texts written before the change read it too; former keys still work) and its badge color, base (working) branch, branch name template ({id}, {tag}, {type}, {slug}; default task/{id}; a branch the worker pushed is followed), commit message template (the commit title of a squash merge by github.merge or bitbucket.merge and of git.land's merge commit; the branch name's fields and {title}, e.g. {tag}: {title}; an empty field drops with its separator; empty: the usual message), On state change (a shell command run in the project's clone on its home machine when a task starts, waits for you, is done, or fails or is stopped, the events ticked; each event once per task, 30 s at most, in the background; WHERDR_TASK_ID, WHERDR_TASK_TAG, WHERDR_TASK_TITLE, WHERDR_TASK_STATE, WHERDR_TASK_PR and WHERDR_PROJECT in its environment, never in its line; exit code and first output lines in the task's log, a failure logged, never retried; set by the user only, a coordinator's or Alfred's change refused; a warning: it runs with your rights on that machine), Archive done tasks after (1, 3, 7, 14, 30 days or Never), Delete the task's branch after its merge (on by default), agents, worktree setup (files copied from the clone such as .env, folders such as node_modules shared only while the lockfile matches the clone's, else a setup command with a time limit; help lines above two columns of fields; the result in the task's log and the worker's instructions, a failure under Your turn with its output), repository visibility, allowed machines and their clone paths (each with its last readiness check, run again with ↻, and a live card: online, offline or paused, hours, a memory bar with agents, the rest, free and the reserve, cores and load or pressure, its agents with task and weight, what it takes now or why not; the board's header opens it), Shown in (the home tab showing it: Automatic with its groups, paused machines left out unless a task runs there, a group, or All tabs; a hint without groups), placement (Heavy to the strongest, Balance the load, Home first, each drawn in a small picture with one line, and the next to-do task with the machine it would go to or why it waits; a task too big for every machine runs on the best one; an idle machine always takes one task its RAM holds, the reserve holds the next ones; a worker started again is heavy only while its step takes screenshots).
- [Workflow tab](docs/project-management.md#workflow): how each task runs, read only: a chart per task type (its route in one line, cards across the width on a computer; each step's holder with its agent and model, how it ends, timeout, proofs, guard; coloured arrows for agents, the engine, your turn and the send-back loop), JSON with Copy, Ask the coordinator to create or change it (a project without a workflow shows only that; Alfred copies another project's workflow by reading it and proposing it); step kinds (landing without a remote merges into the local branch; a merge waits up to 15 minutes for its checks, or for GitHub to show its push, without holding up other tasks; after a merge, the task's remote branch is deleted when safe (merged at its head, no other open PR, not protected, a base, the type's start or the default branch; else kept, with why in the log); [promotion branches](docs/project-management.md#promotion-branches): a task type's `start` (`"start": "develop"`) starts its tasks from that branch's tip on origin (local without origin), pinned at the first start, `{start}` in instructions, a branch missing on the remote makes the task wait for you, never deleted or rewritten, the route line says Starts from develop, an invalid name refused at save, the company example's promote-uat (git.land to uat, then pipeline.watch); Bitbucket Cloud PRs: bitbucket.merge, credentials from the machine; a pipeline watch follows CI or a deploy and wakes the coordinator only on a failure), an accepted change moves tasks under way by step id (a task whose step is gone goes on to the first new step it has not passed; its action runs), Change log, review of the change the coordinator or Alfred proposed (one-line summary, who proposed it, your full request with a link back to it; the proposed workflow's chart with steps added, removed and changed marked in colour, a legend and what changes for the type's tasks, or as a list or JSON), the tab's proposal row with Refuse and Accept as on the card, and its Workflow change card under the turn that proposed it in the coordinator's conversation (where you accept it; a proposal never opens Settings by itself) (that proposal's own changes only, the same chart compact, a tap opens the review; one card per proposal, accepted, refused or replaced); the [reviewer fallback](docs/project-management.md#reviewer-fallback) (prefs reviewFallbackAgent and reviewFallbackModel, together, any pair, none by default, checked at save, also under the project sheet's Agents): the reviewer started instead when the review agent's account is out of quota, near it (5 h at 90 %) or held by its pace, before a start or mid-review (it reviews from the start; a Codex reviewer idle on its usage-limit message counts, its account out until the reset the message gives), each switch in the log and on the Plan's review step, the review agent again once its quota is back; the [review queue](docs/project-management.md#review-queue-and-re-reviews): 2 or 3 reviews at once per reviewer account, the others wait oldest first (*Review waits: 2 ahead on Codex*), shown in `autopilot show`; a later round reviews only the commits since the last one, a merge of the base alone is not reviewed again.
- [Worker and reviewer agents](docs/project-management.md#worker-and-reviewer-agents): a task's `agent`, `reviewAgent` and `reviewFallbackAgent` are `claude`, `codex`, `omp` or a named agent (its command, then the program's arguments; the task starts only on a machine that has it, else waits saying which is missing; unknown names refused at save); one task may override it (`task add`/`task edit --agent`, `--review-agent`), the sheet's History names each run's agent on its start line, `autopilot show` each machine's agents at work; an omp agent is never resumed (a new agent with a handover note), has no quota reading (only the task-count limits pace it) and opens no login incident.
- [Guards](docs/project-management.md#guards): each change saved at once (no Save button); protected branches, who may merge (a waiting merge goes on once wherdr may do it; one you merge on GitHub ends as merged; one cut by a restart goes on by itself), contributor PRs, the project sheet's in-app addresses.
- [Workspaces](docs/workspaces.md): [created](docs/workspaces.md#creating-a-workspace) from Settings › Projects › Add workspace (name, key proposed from it, optional tab group, each machine with its root folder, typed or picked with Browse on that machine's folders (disabled offline), the first its home; nothing cloned; Create adds it and starts its coordinator, whose first reply runs map list and offers to build the map) or by Alfred (`wherdr alfred workspace add <KEY> --root … [--machine …] [--name …] [--group …]`, dry run, --apply or a --propose card); a project of kind workspace (no git itself, its folder a root such as ~/work, in one home tab group; the root may be a git repository, which `wherdr pm repo adopt .` makes a member with its own board, tasks and workflow, its worktrees holding the root's files only (no nested repository; Files to copy and shared folders skip paths in or holding another git repository), no workspace instructions files, a root without origin taking a local-merge workflow only, the coordinator's edits then denied in the whole root) whose coordinator runs linked repositories; each is a member project with no coordinator of its own (its key and task ids shown everywhere as a badge with a dashed border), in one workspace at most, storing only its key, name, color, machine, folder, workspace and visibility; shared settings (machines and the clone root on each, a member's clone being <root>/<repo path>, paused machines, placement, base branch, branch name template, commit message template, On state change command, agents and reviewer fallback, worktree setup, workspace instructions files, archive delay, delete-branch) apply unless the member overrides the field (a cleared base, branch or commit message template or On state change command falls back); workspace instructions files (General tab: the root's AGENTS.md else CLAUDE.md by default, up to 10 paths under the root, or none; their text reaches the worker's and the reviewer's instructions of every member task after the workflow's, under `## Workspace instructions (<file>)`, read again at each start, worker step and review round, a changed one given again with the next step; each cut at 16,000 characters, a cut or missing file logged on the task; the task sheet's Description tab names them; a member inherits, turns them off or replaces them); [workspace skills](docs/workspaces.md#workspace-skills) (General tab: Default, the root's .claude/skills, or None): each root skill linked into every member task's worktree at .claude/skills/<name> before each worker and reviewer start (Claude and omp find it), ignored through git's exclude, read live, the member's own skill of the same name kept, the root member left as is; a workspace has its own workflow (template show/edit on it), which a member without its own runs (its Workflow and Guards tabs show the workspace's, saying so; a member's first accepted or saved workflow becomes its own); the workspace's guards apply to members between the user's and the project's, a member only hardening them; a workspace takes features only, other task types are refused; the workspace's coordinator runs every coordinator command on every member as on the workspace, with no setting, under the same rules (step done/wait/back, task decide, pr merge, ui action/show, automation propose included; --project <member>; never template edit of a member's own workflow), members get no coordinator (none started or listed; the workspace's sidebar row shows under its tab group with its counts (members' tasks and its own features) and its members' key badges, a small square on one with a task waiting; expanded, each member shows its own counts; n waiting for you is a link: one task opens its sheet, several the workspace's board or, on a member, Tasks to review filtered to it), their wakes and Ask the coordinator go to the workspace's coordinator (first line naming the member task), and one autopilot counts At once and Tasks / day across members, Keep the board busy starting their to-do tasks in board order; the workspace map (wherdr pm map show/set/remove, maps/<WS>.json, rendered as map.md in the coordinator's folder) says what each repository does, talks to and is used by, written the first time a task touches a repository (no upfront reading), and map list gives every git repository under the root with an automatic one-line description (manifest description, else the README's first sentence), marked mapped or not, cached a day (--refresh); wherdr pm repo adopt <repo> makes a repository under the root a member with no approval (key and name proposed as the New sheet does, the color its workspace's members use least of the 12 (ties: palette order), shared settings and workflow inherited, never copied (the workspace's coordinator reads which workflow a member runs with template show --project <member>; a member's own workflow is the user's), visibility checked, its map line naming it, written to the workspace's log and listed in the next scheduled wake's health summary), refused outside the root (symlinks resolved on the machine), for a folder already a project or another project's clone there, without git, or without an origin when the workflow pushes or opens PRs; nothing is cloned, a member runs only on machines with its clone at <root>/<repo path> (readiness check, others left out of placement); features (workspace tasks with no agent): wherdr pm feature add, feature split <WS-n> [--from <path>] < plan.json (one call: adopts the repositories needed, adds one sub-task per repository tagged with the feature's id on the board, chains them with after and starts those that wait for nothing, all or nothing, the order's one-line reason kept on the feature; the plan on stdin or from a file under the root with --from, a path outside the root or a link out of it refused), task add --feature [--refs T1,T2], task edit --after (after across the workspace's projects, no cycle, no link outside it); mergeAfter (plan mergeAfter, task add/edit --merge-after, same rules) makes a sub-task's PR wait out of line in its merge queue (waits for LED-4 to be done) until those tasks are done (whole workflow: merged and deploy watched), the rest of the queue merging meanwhile, its sheet saying Merges once LED-4 is done; a stopped or abandoned upstream keeps it waiting and wakes the workspace's coordinator once; a promotion across a feature's repositories: one promote sub-task per repository (a type with `start`) with --merge-after mirroring the feature's order; feature close [--anyway] once every sub-task is done or abandoned, refused while lines of the feature's plan file are still unticked (listed) unless --anyway; [plan lines](docs/workspaces.md#plan-lines): a split may name the spec's tasks.md ("plan", a path under the root, shown by show as planFile) and each sub-task the lines it covers ("refs": IDs like T010, shown by show, given to the worker as "Plan lines: T010 in <path>"); once a sub-task with refs is done (whole workflow, abandoned excluded) the engine itself ticks each ref's first open line `- [ ] T010` → `- [x] T010 … (done: PA-1, <merge sha>, <date>)` on the workspace's machine, a line already ticked or not found left and logged, and in a git root commits that file only (git commit --only, no git hook, the workspace's commit message template else "WS-1: tick T010 (PA-1)") when the file has no uncommitted change and the root is on its base branch (the root member's, else the workspace's, else origin's default; none known: not committed), an edit hidden by assume-unchanged or skip-worktree counting as a local change, else nothing is written, the reason logged (planTick), a notification to the user and a wake to the coordinator (autopilot on); a lock, a merge or rebase under way or a file changed meanwhile is retried (every 5 min, 12 times or an hour), a detached HEAD, another branch, local changes, an untracked file, a file of another repository (a member's clone) or a failed or slow commit is final; only - * + bullets outside fenced code count, an ID matched whole, dates in UTC; a root with no git just gets the file written; a feature's state is derived: to do, working, waiting for you, done; [Context folders](docs/workspaces.md#context-folders): read-only snapshots of other members of a task's workspace for its worker and reviewer; `context` (`all` or member keys) on a task type, or `task add --context` / `task edit --context` (a task's own wins; `none` off; `""` back to the type's; refused outside a workspace, for a non-member and the task's own project); the first start fetches each member's base branch and makes a detached read-only worktree at <home>/.wherdr/pm/context/<member>/<commit>, shared by the machine's tasks; later starts and the reviewer keep those commits; a *Context (read only)* section in the instructions and a `context:` log line ((not fetched), (local branch), skipped members with their reason, never blocking); `--add-dir` per folder for Claude and omp, none for Codex; the worktree sweep removes snapshots no unfinished task reads and unused for an hour.
- [Automations](docs/project-management.md#automations): tasks added on a schedule or an event; the coordinator or Alfred proposes them, you accept or refuse; a list with each one's trigger in words, next firing and last results.
- [Who sends a wake](docs/project-management.md#who-sends-a-wake): each wake's first line and chat tag name its source: Autopilot (its scheduled wake, `Autopilot: scheduled wake`, on Every: the goal and the health summary, done, waiting for you, stalled, idle machines, acked at once when all is well; none with the autopilot off; Every empty or off: no interval wake, stalls then only through engine wakes; an older Health check interval joined Every once, the shorter kept), Step check (a held step's start, recheck or timeout, even with the autopilot off; rechecks with no news back off 5m, 10m, 20m, 40m up to 1h and start over on any news on the task; the coordinator postpones with `wherdr pm step wait <task> --for <duration>|--until-user --reason`; the task sheet shows the next recheck; past the step's time limit or waiting until you write, its To do tab says what waits, for how long and the coordinator's last wait reason, with Ask the coordinator, your message to it that starts the rechecks over, then Asked), Engine (a block given up after failed fixes), Incident; in the conversation a wake is a compact muted row (tag, first reason, time; tap for the full text and turn, which ends at its own end, at your next message or `!`/`/` command, or where the coordinator speaks on its own after a background task), not a bubble, with the coordinator's answer under it, muted when a routine one-liner, else in full like any message (a `wherdr` block, a link, more than one line or a question never folds); consecutive routine wakes fold into one row (3 routine checks · last: "…", 08:00–11:00; its task chips wrap inside the row, the conversation never scrolls sideways), holding only the wakes and their own turns, a message of yours Claude took in the same turn as a wake its own bubble (photos included) beside the wake's row, that turn's answer in full, no wake sent while your message is being typed, an incident or an answer asking you stays visible in its stronger colour; routine events switched per project (a new one: Task done and Task stuck on), judgment always wakes the coordinator; one kind per wake, the same ack. Skipped, and listed by `autopilot show`: a scheduled wake while nothing it could act on changed and its health lines say nothing new (12 h at most), an Engine wake for a block that is only an offline or paused machine, a second wake for a question already answered with `tell`.
- [Autopilot](docs/project-management.md#autopilot): when the project works without you, each project's own (Alfred has none), the clock header button (no workflow proposals) and its window (880 px on a computer), the autopilot's switch and state above two tabs remembered per device: Settings (answering agent, then grouped: goal (optional; empty: wakes say none is set), when it wakes (Every with its hint: empty, no timed wake, only the events; a timed wake skipped while nothing is new, one per 12 h at most, unless Look for new work; and Routines: a list with Add routine, each a row with when (day chips, Every day / Weekdays, a time; Advanced: a cron), its own goal, a switch and Delete, editable in place; at its time a wake Routine: <goal> with the health summary, within the hours and pace, skipped when off; an older At became one routine with the goal; a routine wakes the coordinator, an automation adds a task; `autopilot show` lists them), limits, hours (new projects: Tasks / day unlimited and At once Auto, pace and machine room still hold automatic work; limits and hours hold automatic work only: a start you ask for goes past them, with a word, and still counts; a hint on the older 10 / 2; the events it also wakes on, a switch each with what the coordinator does: Task done (start what follows, tell you, update notes) and Task stuck (unblock before the engine's two failed fixes) on for a new project, Ready for you and Task added off, an existing project keeps its choice; Task added wakes only for tasks added by someone else than this coordinator; a pinned bar with Cancel and Save, enabled by a change; leaving the tab or closing with unsaved changes asks; a project.autopilot link opens Settings) and Activity (no Open button, the coordinator's row and header open it; Start with … only when no row can start it; counts, Wake now with its hint (wakes the coordinator now with its goal), the day's timeline (24 h bar with its hours shaded, wakes sent and skipped with why, tasks started, now and the next wake; the worker's account pace gauge, go or what it waits for; the events listed, yesterday's below); Keep the board busy: the engine starts the next to-do task itself while a machine has room; the coordinator's view of machines and weights (`autopilot show`; weights learned from measured memory peaks after 3 runs; `show <task>`, `--on`, `--weight`).
- [What a task's agent said](docs/project-management.md#what-a-tasks-agent-said): `wherdr pm read`, an agent's last message or question from any machine, and the question in the wake.
- [Board](docs/project-management.md#board): the project picker (Follow machine tab, the default once groups exist; All projects; one project, shown as its key badge in its color then its name, as in every project picker; kept across devices), columns (card shapes until the board is first read; a done or archived task is never under Your turn; Done shows only tasks not archived, newest first, its footer *N archived · show* opens the archived tasks, searchable, newest first; a task is archived after its project's delay (a feature's sub-task only once its feature is closed), 7 days by default, and Unarchive brings it back), a workspace picked shows its features and all its members' tasks (sub-tasks folded into their feature's card unless *Sub-tasks in their columns too*), cards (the id badge copies the id; the task's machine when its project allows several), time in the step and total time, Add task (with its weight: Auto, Light, Standard, Heavy), Start, Start on another machine (its readiness check), Stop, Delete (a task never started, also one whose start failed before its worktree, its error on the card until deleted or started again); a refused merge said in plain words (a conflict the agent is already fixing leaves Your turn).
- [What agents show in the chat](docs/project-management.md#what-agents-show-in-the-chat): every agent's *Showing instead of telling* table (situation → tool, with an example): choices, a `questions` card for several questions at once (never a numbered list) and task cards for all, plus highlights, status cards, action buttons, screenshots and proposed settings for Alfred and coordinators; one card per message, blocks only in a wake, the link after a refusal, never "done" before the card says so.
- [Coordinators on other projects](docs/project-management.md#coordinators-on-other-projects): the General tab's Other projects this coordinator may act on (Off by default, Read: list, show, read, plan, incidents; Act: also task add/start/stop/edit/note/order/tag/link/check/remove, tell, report back/close), a task id names its project, `--project <KEY>` on list, plan, incidents and task add; guards, merges, approvals, settings, autopilot, workflow and automations never; the refusal names the setting; logged with the acting coordinator's name, the other coordinator told at its next wake, listed in its instructions.
- [Coordinators' notes](docs/project-management.md#coordinators-notes): `wherdr pm notes …`, a coordinator's notes: any note listed, edited, moved or removed; `notes add` defaults to the home tab its project shows in
- [Board order](docs/project-management.md#board-order): cards in board order (the coordinator's `wherdr pm task order` first, then oldest first), shared by everyone and kept across restarts; Keep the board busy, the merge queue and `wherdr pm list` follow it.
- [Spec changes](docs/project-management.md#spec-changes): when you change your mind mid-task, the coordinator's `wherdr pm task edit` (title, description, reason, diff in the log), `task note` and `tell --spec`; the worker and the reviewer read every note, the latest overriding the description; shown under the description in the task sheet; never in a wake; after several send-backs, the coordinator's `task decide <task> pass` on findings that contradict a spec change its reason cites (date or words), never before a guarded merge nor on a critical finding, written to the task's log, and the coordinator tells you in its next message.
- [Tasks that touch the same files](docs/project-management.md#tasks-that-touch-the-same-files): declared files (files.txt, task add --files), changed files counted from the fork with the base (a merged base never counts), the start that waits behind a task with the same files, Start anyway.
- [Task sheet](docs/project-management.md#task-sheet): opens over the current page from Tasks to handle or a chat task link (`?task=ID`, kept on reload); a close cross at the header's top right; the id badge by the title (copies the id; a long title two lines at most on a phone, whole on a tap, one line once scrolled or typing), which branch merges into which (the board card too when it is not the project's working branch), the task's PR as a badge on that line with its state (open, merged, closed, conflict, red CI; new tab; wraps under on a phone; in the sheet's header once the line scrolls away; none before a PR, not repeated under the description), the task's total time at its end, the buttons that make sense now (the step's own first: Merge, Approve…; Stop only while the agent holding the step runs, not at a merge step; Open the agent whatever the step: the step's agent if it runs, else the worker, Worker or Reviewer in a menu when both run, disabled with Agent is terminated once it ended; a ⋯ menu with Check on GitHub, also `wherdr pm task check`, for a stuck merge step or an archived task's PR, and Report a problem) and its Description (Markdown), Plan (proofs in Markdown, folded, each once; a commit as a short sha linked to the Git host; a PR link as PR #12), Comments (the worker's and the reviewer's reports and verdicts in order, Markdown, folded) and History (time per step, waits for you, review rounds and CI fixes on top, then the whole log as a timeline: when, who and what per event, a square mark by kind (started, done, sent back, merged, failed, your action), hand-offs, catch-ups, CI fixes, routine lines lighter) tabs, in one scroll; on a task waiting for you, To do opens on a [TL;DR](docs/project-management.md#tldr) by Claude Haiku (at most five lines in plain words, no code names: what changes for you, what to look at on the screenshots, anything wrong; not how it was checked nor the Merge; written again once on a new prompt version, otherwise only on new commits of its own or new findings, not on a base merge, rebase or CI re-run; skipped while the pace holds automatic work, the notes shown then; an agent's question gets two or three plain lines of its own, once per question), the screenshots under it, and a link to Comments.
- [A task waiting for you](docs/project-management.md#a-task-waiting-for-you): the To do tab, Merge, Send back (or the coordinator's `wherdr pm step back <task> "<what to change>" --user-said "<your words>"` when you tell it the changes: same send-back, your turn only, never in a wake, only on a step that waits for you; the task leaves Tasks to review until its next review), Try again (each try's result in History; unreadable PR details read again, then the error with the output's last lines) and other answers; Ask the agent to fix it on a block its worker could fix (a failed action such as a conflict or red checks, a stalled or ended worker, a step past its time limit; Try again then secondary; an action failed outside the code, herdr-core, a machine, the network or the Git host, has only Try again, first, its reason with herdr-core's kind and hint; an unknown failure has Try again first, the agent second): the worker, started again if it ended, gets the block's reason, fixes it or asks you one question with choices; the task leaves Your turn at once (the agent is fixing it), back only on its question or the fix's new failure; your own action, logged as asked the agent to fix: <reason>; a stalled review (past its time limit, or its reviewer gone without a verdict) said in one sentence, with Restart the review (a new reviewer on the PR's latest commit), and the card's status says review pending, not ready to merge, until the review passes; a PR you merge on your Git host (I merged it, and what to do when it is not merged yet); Open the PR at the merge step for a PR a step gave as its link proof (GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab, Azure DevOps), also on the card as PR #12; screenshots of the result taken last, each with its commit (one from before the last commit stays shown, marked Earlier commit); a redone screenshot replaces only the one it redoes (&replaces=<file>, the old one under Earlier screenshots), a send-back keeps the set and lists the picked ones to redo, then Since your last look (Tasks to review and To do) quotes your note with each screenshot taken since beside the version it redoes, a round with fewer screenshots than the last ends only with a Fewer screenshots because: … line; new screenshots after a rework (new commits since the review) marked after rework; a waiting PR kept up to date with its base (off Your turn and Tasks to handle while it is updated, its conflict solved or its checks fixed, with a neutral line; back once GitHub reads it clean), an approved merge that goes on by itself once ready (kept across updates, asked again only on new screenshots or interface changes; comment-only changes (strings and spaces still count), base merges with the same own interface change and fixes outside interface files keep it, each said in the log as approval kept: …; when it is dropped the log says why (files and commits, or new screenshots), the agent is asked why and uploads new screenshots with a Back to review because: … line (&reason= on the upload), shown in a banner on top of Tasks to review and the To do tab (a task it names is a link; the engine's files and commits until it answers); comment-only changes start no new review round either; Merge stays loading on the card and the sheet until it merges or fails, with what it waits for, the same after a reload), and the project's merge queue (ready PRs merge in turn, a PR needing work steps out of line, updates only on a conflict or when GitHub requires them, all in one pass, the agent's fix pushed whatever the place, idle agents released; its place or why it stepped out on the card); a tap on Your turn or Tasks to handle opens the asking agent's conversation, else the sheet; on a phone its buttons stay pinned at the bottom of the tab, hidden while you type in a field of the sheet so nothing covers it.
- [Tasks to review, one at a time](docs/project-management.md#tasks-to-review): opens from Home's card, the board's **To review** (its count, the same) or a link `#/review` (the former `#/decisions` and the grouped notification too, over the page shown); a task to approve with its id badge (copies the id), TL;DR, newest screenshots, PR and verdict in one line, then Approve (the merge's Accept: *Approved* on the button, then the next one slides in; a fade with reduced motion; a failure stays with its error) or Reject (a note, the screenshots that are wrong and your own, file or paste, sent back to its worker, each screenshot a download with the task's key); an agent's question shows its Haiku summary, the full question folded (Markdown, as in the chat, never cut), its choices as buttons and Another answer with Send (sent to the agent, then the next task) and Open the task; a question answered anywhere (here, its conversation, a coordinator's tell) leaves at once; anything else that waits (another step of yours too) shows its To do answers (choices, Try again) and Open the task; a block its worker could fix has Ask the agent to fix it first (only Try again for a failure outside the code) (The agent is fixing it, then off the list until its question or a new failure); every task has Open the agent (as on the task sheet); 3 of 12 with previous and next (a task passed over stays), a stable order while open (new tasks at the end; the one on screen never swapped, handled elsewhere it stays with a muted Handled elsewhere line until you move on), every button that sends (Approve, Send back, a choice, Send, Ask the coordinator…) loads alone from the tap until the server answered, the others disabled, then says it went through (a check, *Sent back*); keys → ← A R, All done after the last (grouped in the middle, the window shrunk to it on a computer); on a computer a 960 px window up to 90 % high, screenshots two per row, only the content scrolls; filter Follow group tab, All, a group or a project, each with its count of tasks waiting (a muted grey chip after its name, none at 0, those with tasks first), kept across devices.
- [Notes on a task waiting for you](docs/project-management.md#notes-on-a-task-waiting-for-you): the To do tab's Worker's note (the closing report, report.md with one section per round, the first report never replaced) and Reviewer's note (verdict, what was fixed during the rounds, what is left as minor), in Markdown, folded, with Show more, the task's summary above the worker's note, full width one above the other (Worker / Reviewer tabs on a phone).
- [Report a problem](docs/project-management.md#report-a-problem): tell the coordinator what is wrong with a task waiting for you, block its merge, withdraw.
- [What wherdr fixes on its own](docs/project-management.md#what-wherdr-fixes-on-its-own): a conflict with the base (to the worker), red CI (an infrastructure error in the log run again once, else to the worker), a push refused as behind its remote (synced, pushed again), a merge fixed after the fact by the clone's `wherdr.afterMerge` command, a PR updated on GitHub included (wherdr's docs/llms.txt: one line per entry), an interrupted action (run again), a stalled agent, a task nobody moves (one task's error never stops the others; quiet 20 min with no stated reason: its stuck or never-started action, or its merge, run again, looked at after 40, 80 min…, the coordinator woken once per step; a hung step action freed after 30 min, its late result only logged); the coordinator woken once after 2 failed tries, with what was tried, and with Task stuck on (a new project's default) also as the block begins.
- [A stalled task](docs/project-management.md#a-stalled-task): red CI or an idle agent: one nudge, a restart 10 min later, the coordinator woken 10 min after that, then Tasks to review and a notification after 30 min; a stall or a step past its time limit leaves Tasks to review once the task is back to work (on a coordinator-held step, Ask the coordinator does it: Waiting for the coordinator to check the deploy, then Asked); a step's time limit stops counting while its machine is offline, an incident is open, the task waits for room or its agent waits for your answer to a question or permission (the card shows what it waits for). [A task waiting for another task](docs/project-management.md#a-task-waiting-for-another-task): a worker's `blocked:on <task|repo>: <need>` parks its task (an after link, its agents ended, no stall, nudge or restart, *Waits for WHR-12: <need>* on the card, one coordinator wake); resumed in the same conversation with the other task's title, PR and report once it is done; a cycle is refused with one decision wake (shared contract task or merge the two), unanswered, you get the *coordinator is not answering* notification. [A task paused for room](docs/project-management.md#a-task-paused-for-room): `wherdr pm task stop <task> --for-room --reason …` (a coordinator, in a user turn or a wake) parks a started task to free its machine: no agent, *Paused: waiting for room on <machine>* on its card, never in Tasks to review or Your turn; the engine continues it in the same conversation once the machine has room, in board order, before new tasks start there, keeping the cap; a paused or parked task takes no At once slot; its start failing 3 times (not for room) ends the pause: it waits with the real reason, the coordinator woken; its sheet has Resume now and Stop.
- [Why agents are gone](docs/project-management.md#why-agents-are-gone): the engine's cause from facts (machine offline, herdr-core or wherdr restarted, agent killed or crashed, out of memory, account limit, login expired, unknown), recorded as an incident per machine; an agent on its login prompt is a login incident, not a permission: one per account and machine, one Home notice (Claude login expired on <machine>, Open a terminal there, I logged in), its tasks off Tasks to review; `wherdr pm incidents [--since]`, the last open one in `autopilot show`.
- [The engine resumes the work](docs/project-management.md#the-engine-resumes-the-work): a task an incident stopped waits for wherdr (not Your turn) and is resumed once the cause is gone (restart or crash at once, machine back online, account limit reset, login renewed: the credentials file changed or I logged in, each stuck agent restarted one per machine and minute, then told once to continue where it stopped): its worker in its worktree, Claude's conversation resumed, else a new agent with a handover; the tasks before it first, its followers *Waits for <task> to resume*; placement, room and pace held, one worker per task; the same cause again within an hour of a resume is not resumed again.
- [The incident wake](docs/project-management.md#the-incident-wake): one wake per incident (not per task) once the engine's resumes settle, to each project's coordinator and to Alfred for all projects: the cause and its evidence, what was resumed, what still waits and why (machine offline, limit until <time>), what needs the coordinator or the user; never state a cause not read: `wherdr pm incidents`, `autopilot show`, `read <task>` first, else 'unknown' and what was checked.
- [A task's temporary files](docs/project-management.md#a-tasks-temporary-files): `.wherdr-tmp` in the task's worktree (TMPDIR, CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR, NODE_COMPILE_CACHE), ignored by git, removed with the worktree; no agent started while /tmp has under 500 MB free; [a done task's worktree](docs/project-management.md#a-done-tasks-worktree): removed once its agents ended (killing what works in it, `git worktree remove` then prune, size freed in the task's log), its local branch too when Delete the task's branch after its merge is on (archived: kept); the commit a merge step recorded as merged covers squash-merged commits, a later one still keeps it; kept while not done, an agent runs, with uncommitted changes, unpushed and unmerged commits, or outside the pm worktrees folder; a sweep at start and every few hours removes the leftovers; a removal has 10 minutes and locks the worktree against prune, one left halfway (tracked files only deleted) is finished, one with a changed or new file or locked by you stays.
- [Processes an agent leaves behind](docs/project-management.md#processes-an-agent-leaves-behind): ending an agent kills its terminal's process tree and groups (TERM, then KILL after 3 s); every 5 minutes and at start, processes an agent started (known by the task's .wherdr-tmp they inherit, never by their folder alone; on macOS, sh/zsh/sleep with their marked parent or group, or re-parented in the task's worktree; never the user's own shells, apps or daemons) are killed once their task has no live agent, and logged on the task; removing a worktree kills what works in it first; a CPU guard kills a task's process above 80 % CPU for 20 min after its agent ended (tells the coordinator while it runs); Settings › Machines says *n leftover processes killed*; the wherdr template's workers run test commands that could hang with a timeout.
- [Alfred's command](docs/alfred.md): `wherdr alfred`, what Alfred reads and changes after your yes in a turn of your own message (`--apply` refused otherwise; guards by a card only) or a card's Apply (told back to it, so it goes on by itself; projects, workspaces, their machines, guards, coordinators started or resumed, lines added to a coordinator's memory.md, settings, custom themes, all v2 projects in one card), the workflow changes it proposes for your review, and its messages to a project's coordinator (`tell`, `last`); [requests about a project](docs/alfred.md#requests-about-a-project): Alfred finds the project (name, key or the open tab's; buttons when unsure), relays it to its coordinator as *From Alfred, for the user* (the coordinator adds the task, Alfred never changes the project; the relay is never your yes: no step ended, PR merged or spec changed on it), waits (`last` lists the tasks added since) and reports back in a line or two with each task as a task card; for a long back-and-forth it suggests the coordinator's conversation.
- [Agents of a task that waits for you](docs/project-management.md#agents-of-a-task-that-waits-for-you): an agent on its login prompt waits for the login (an incident), not for you; idle agents ended (after 10 minutes idle; 30 after your last message to one, from its chat or terminal; never while its conversation is open; memory short for a task waiting to start cuts that grace, logged) and started again, Open the agent on a released worker (task sheet, Tasks to review) asks first in a dialog (closed at 12:43 to free memory on its machine, its conversation comes back as it was; Reopen or Cancel), then starts it again with its conversation and no message (no model turn until you write; Claude and Codex; omp, or a Codex conversation not found, starts a new one with the handover), at once when you answer (a decision, Send back, Try again), a worker that ended too; a watchdog starts again the agent of a task under way missing for 3 minutes (after a restart too; a start herdr-core never confirmed is found by its labels after a minute, else counted missing), else the card says why and the coordinator is woken once at the second failure; kept while the worker updates the PR (a catch-up, a CI fix), a worker that ended started again with that work (once), else the card says why it waits (its machine offline or paused, no room on it, its agent ended) and the coordinator is woken (none: Your turn; no room: only after 30 minutes of it), unpushed commits pushed first; which agent a coordinator's `tell` reaches (--to worker|reviewer); in a wake, `tell --fix base|ci|machine|stall --reason` unblocks a mechanical block (autopilot on, twice per task and step, logged; at any step an ended worker starts again with it while its worktree is there; at the review step a reviewer not running starts the review again), a permission request stays yours; a failed step action handed over with `--fix` leaves Tasks to review (*the agent is fixing it*), is tried again once the worker is done, and comes back with the new reason if it fails again or the worker stops without a report. One worker and one reviewer per task: a second start at once is refused (already starting), a held start dropped, a duplicate agent ended and logged.
- [Notes](docs/alfred.md#notes): `wherdr alfred notes` and `wherdr pm notes` (list, show, add, edit, remove, file put, file remove): short whiteboard notes agents write and the user reads (at most 12 content lines: blank lines, `---` separators and headings do not count; 1500 characters), scoped to all or one home tab (a group or a machine shown as its own tab), linking to other notes, files under `notes/` or in-app places, with project badges `[[KEY-12]]` and custom badges `[[label|icon|colour|link]]`; any coordinator may list, edit, move and remove any note, adding to its project's tab by default, and changes another project's note only when outdated or asked; every change logged with who made it
- [Suggestions](docs/alfred.md#suggestions): Alfred and coordinators suggest a setting you may like once (`ui open --target`), never again if ignored; when wherdr cannot do what you need, they may draft an issue or PR on wherdr's repository, with no private data, posted only on your yes.
- [Updating wherdr](docs/alfred.md#updating-wherdr): the banner's Update with Alfred sends `Update wherdr to <version>: <release URL>`; for any update Alfred reads update-with-an-agent.md and the release notes, never from memory.
- [After an update](docs/alfred.md#after-an-update): new instructions for Alfred and coordinators, and the one-line notice on their next command (also after a rebuild from a new commit); they read the running build's docs wherever wherdr was started from; Alfred gives the server's real address and port, and server commands as text to copy, never *Run*. A coordinator on another machine reads the running wherdr's docs with `wherdr pm docs [<page>[#<section>]]` (the index, a page, one section; read-only, in a wake too).

## Machines, quotas and notifications

- [Several machines](docs/machines.md#several-machines-ssh): machines reached by hc over SSH; the host shown by its host name with a HOST badge; New preselects a machine of the current tab.
- [Before adding a machine](docs/machines.md#before-adding-a-machine): what a machine needs first.
- [Manage machines](docs/machines.md#manage-machines): Settings › Machines (one card per machine: name, state, actions, keep awake, memory), add (the Add machine button at the top: a window with the SSH target and name, then a confirmation; an error keeps it open), reconnect, rename, forget, keep awake (until a time or turned off, laptop battery and lid warning, a loader on the button, could not reach vs not available), capacity (memory, cores, load on Linux and macOS; swap on Linux; on macOS memory pressure first, then macOS's own available estimate, its free percentage of the RAM, with a 10 % reserve), memory limits (an idle machine always takes one task its RAM holds, the minimum free holds the next ones), available hours and offline machines (an automatic start that finds its machine unreachable waits and starts once it is back), and where each start goes (placement across a project's machines).
- [Pause a machine for a project](docs/machines.md#pause-a-machine-for-a-project): a machine's on/off switch in a project's Machines list: no new task there, running ones finish, clone kept; Paused in every project in Settings › Machines.
- [Claude and Codex quotas](docs/quotas.md#claude-and-codex-quotas): remaining usage per account, with the machines sharing it (a Claude Ultra account shows its week alone as one bar across the row, no 5-hour window; account name and machine chips on one line; one Codex account stays one row when a machine is idle; a failed read keeps the machine's last good reading, with its age, while reads fail), and its setup; a value no longer known (reset since the reading, or read longer ago than its window) shows ? on a dashed bar, how to refresh it on hover or tap; a Codex 'Limit reached' past its reset reads as reset, credits show and let work go on; one read over an hour ago is muted ('may have reset'), refreshed through Codex's read-only limits read (at most every 15 min per account), and lets one automatic start through instead of holding work. [Codex updates](docs/quotas.md#codex-updates): Codex starts with its update check off; a message sent while it installs or updates waits and is typed once it is ready, even after a restart of wherdr, held once even when sent again (back into the field if it exits, or if typing it timed out); a Codex that exits after updating itself keeps its space, with a Your turn card (Resume conversation, Start fresh).
- [Pace](docs/quotas.md#pace): Settings › Agents › Pace, its modes (Free, the default, stops only at the account's own limit), each account's weekly chart (usage since the last reset from the pacing log, the target line or reserve limit, now; Free usage only; no readings: a gap), when automatic work may start, and the end-of-week burn (one switch: no pace limit until the weekly reset, then off); a reviewer account held by its pace hands new reviews to the reviewer fallback.
- [Notifications](docs/notifications.md#notifications): Web Push and Do not disturb.
- [A default and exceptions](docs/notifications.md#a-default-and-exceptions): one synced policy: a default and its exceptions, a coordinator's kept across restarts.
- [Notifications on hc](docs/core.md#notifications): when v3 sends a push, from hc's events.

## Extending and fixing

- [Plugins](docs/plugins.md#wherdr-plugins): optional page plugins and how to install them; they load only once the [Community plugins switch](docs/plugins.md#community-plugins-switch) (server-wide, off by default, full-access warning; existing installs with plugins stay on; off while settings.json cannot be read) is on. [Install one from GitHub](docs/plugins.md#install-from-github) (`owner/repo[@ref]`, exact commit and warning shown before Install; Check for update installs only on Update, which leaves the switch as it is; Remove); [publish one](docs/plugins.md#publish-a-plugin-on-github).
- [The plugin module](docs/plugins.md#the-module): what a plugin file exports (`apiVersion: 1`, [drafts](docs/plugins.md#drafts-wherdrdraft) `get`/`set`/`insert`/`focus` which never send, `currentAgent`, `onNavigate`, [header actions](docs/plugins.md#header-actions-wherdrmountheaderaction) `mountHeaderAction`) and [lifecycle](docs/plugins.md#lifecycle-and-failure-isolation) (idempotent disposers, automatic cleanup on stop/error/update even without `deactivate()`, guarded callbacks).
- [Markers](docs/plugins.md#markers-data-wherdr): `data-wherdr` markers (`composer-actions`, `header-actions`, zero-width when empty and measured by header folding…).
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md#troubleshooting): hc connection, conversations, machines and network problems.
- [Setup on hc](docs/core.md#setup): `HC_SOCKET`, the hc endpoint wherdr talks to.

## Contributors

- [Development and tests](docs/development.md): run from source and test.
- [Design rules](docs/design.md): the interface styling reference, sheets included (where focus goes on open); a choice among 2 to 4 options in Settings is a compact segmented button (SettingsChoice, a UToggleGroup in wherdr's square style: as wide as its options, one row, chosen option filled with the accent; a growing list turns into a select past 4), 5+ a select, on/off a switch; nothing scrolls sideways (no negative horizontal margin without an `overflow-safe` reason); one scroll per sheet, which ends at the sheet's bottom edge (the bottom gap is padding inside it); Home's list likewise runs to the bottom under the floating + New, no footer band; the app's thin scrollbars, never the browser's.
- [Dictation design](docs/dictation.md): the dictation engines and how to add one; the on-device model cards (each model's best languages and their quality, the device's language marked; Qwen3-ASR 0.6B q4f16 opt-in on WebGPU with shader-f16, using `ort` and pane terms); why a server-side model install fails (missing decompressor, disk full; .tar.bz2 needs no bzip2, a JS decoder unpacks it); read aloud and its voices (iOS gives web apps only its standard voices); the neural voice catalog (Siwis, Cori, MLS) and its engine (streamed WebAudio playback, fallback to the device's voices); the Voice of wherdr setting (install a French or English voice, each reply read in its guessed language).
- [Read aloud: the voice of wherdr](docs/read-aloud.md): off by default, a Play button under each reply once a voice is chosen (a voice chosen earlier on the device is kept); the on-device voices (Siwis, Cori, MLS), their licences and the attribution shown; espeak-ng (GPL) inside the pinned sherpa-onnx 1.12.x runtime; the memory budget (measured heap, else an estimate); the iPhone 13 measurements of Siwis and Cori (load, first sentence, real-time factor; Heap is the runtime's 512 MiB WASM memory, not the voice's own use); how to measure with Test (download, load, first sentence, real-time factor, heap).

## v2 only

- [The wherdr command](docs/command.md): the 2.x npm and Homebrew packages and service.
- [Migrate from a 1.x Docker install](docs/migrate-from-1.x-docker.md): Docker to the native 2.0 service.
- [Releasing](docs/RELEASING.md): release process of 3.x (the main line: GitHub release only, marked latest, optional `## Upgrade notes` in its notes, then bump `v3` to the next `-dev`) and 2.x fixes (npm, Homebrew, never latest), and the v2 → v3 transition plan.
